overview: Two quick bench tests that, run in sequence, take an unknown Gram-positive coccus most of the way to a genus and species.

aspects.label: Overview / Core Definition
aspects.valueA: Detects the enzyme catalase, which breaks down hydrogen peroxide into water and oxygen gas (visible bubbling).
aspects.valueB: Detects the enzyme coagulase, which clots plasma by converting fibrinogen to fibrin.

aspects.label: Principle
aspects.valueA: A drop of hydrogen peroxide is added to a bacterial colony; bubbles indicate a positive result.
aspects.valueB: Bacterial growth is mixed with rabbit or human plasma; visible clotting indicates a positive result.

aspects.label: Purpose
aspects.valueA: First distinguishes Staphylococcus (positive) from Streptococcus/Enterococcus (negative) among Gram-positive cocci.
aspects.valueB: Distinguishes Staphylococcus aureus (positive) from coagulase-negative staphylococci like S. epidermidis.

aspects.label: Typical Use
aspects.valueA: Run on any Gram-positive, catalase-relevant coccus isolate.
aspects.valueB: Run specifically on catalase-positive, Gram-positive cocci already identified as staphylococci.

aspects.label: Result Reading
aspects.valueA: Immediate — bubbling is seen within seconds.
aspects.valueB: Slower — tube method may need up to 24 hours; slide method gives a rapid but less sensitive result.

aspects.label: Common Pitfalls
aspects.valueA: False positives from red blood cells on the loop if pulled from blood agar; false negatives with old cultures.
aspects.valueB: Slide (bound) coagulase can miss free coagulase; a negative slide test should be confirmed with a tube test.

aspects.label: Sequence in Identification Workflow
aspects.valueA: Performed first, right after Gram stain confirms Gram-positive cocci in clusters.
aspects.valueB: Performed second, only after catalase confirms the isolate is a Staphylococcus.

aspects.label: Key Distinguishing Feature
aspects.valueA: Splits Gram-positive cocci into Staphylococcus vs Streptococcus/Enterococcus.
aspects.valueB: Splits staphylococci into S. aureus vs coagulase-negative species.

overlay.examHighYieldNote: Catalase first, then coagulase — the classic two-step staph identification pathway.
